# File permissions in Linux

## Project description

 I worked through linux using bash to manage user permissions using chmod commands and user permission arguments on project files and their access to certain directories. I then ensured all changes were made and correct by using the ls -la command.

## Check file and directory details

<img width="1087" height="313" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2c8f694-ef0c-470f-ba6d-b6f8cbc33b3d" />

I began with navigating to the directory where user permissions needed to be altered by using the command (cd). The directory I needed to go to was the projects directory. I used the ls -la command to show me all users, groups and others and display their current permissions

## Describe the permissions string

<img width="155" height="25" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7870bf74-56e8-4fc6-98f1-efeb30bc8214" />

The permission string is a 10 character string. It is split into three sections of three characters. Character 2-4 are the user, character 5-7 are the group and 8-10 are other. Each section represents a User, group or other. The first section of the string begins with the letter d, this is for directory. The letters that follow, rwx are their permissions for the files and directories. R is for read, w is for write and x is for execute. After drwx there is an r.  r-x means the group has read and execute permissions but no write permissions. The final three characters r-x are the same permissions as the group. However this section of the string is the other permissions. 

## Change file permissions

<img width="1087" height="541" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13e535e9-1334-4f33-be0b-58eecdb5d940" />

Here I needed to change the “other” permissions on project\_k. Other needed to have their write privileges removed. By using the chmod command followed by the argument o-w I successfully removed its write privileges. 

## Change file permissions on a hidden file

<img width="1086" height="257" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0cdb084-6688-415e-9bbc-6fb20901a25e" />

The .project\_x.txt file was an archived file which is why it was hidden. By using the ls -la command I was able to show all files and directories including hidden ones. Project\_x had permissions that allowed the user as well as the group to write to it, they should only have read permissions. By using the chmod u-w,g-w command and argument I was able to remove the write permission from both simultaneously. 

## Change directory permissions

<img width="1086" height="226" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b466a896-d685-4533-9d58-53b50c732a51" />

Next I had to remove execute permissions for the group. The group had access to the drafts directory when only the user, (researcher2) should have access. I used the chmod command followed by the argument g-x then ending with the input of the current directory to remove execute permissions from the group.

## Summary

In this lab I demonstrated my understanding of changing user permissions to files, hidden files and directories. By using chmod commands and user permission arguments u+w, g-x, o-rwx I was able to successfully add and remove permissions. I then made sure my inputs were correct by using the ls -la command to show user permissions again and see that my permission changes were correct.
